Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that sends failed messages to a dead-letter destination using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 2 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 3 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 4 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 5 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from typing import Optional

import boto3
from botocore.exceptions import BotoCoreError, ClientError


class DeadLetterMessenger:
    def __init__(
        self,
        source_queue_url: str,
        dead_letter_queue_url: str,
        region_name: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.source_queue_url = source_queue_url
        self.dead_letter_queue_url = dead_letter_queue_url
        self.sqs = boto3.client("sqs", region_name=region_name)

    def receive_and_process(self, max_messages: int = 10) -> int:
        response = self.sqs.receive_message(
            QueueUrl=self.source_queue_url,
            MaxNumberOfMessages=max(1, min(max_messages, 10)),
            WaitTimeSeconds=20,
            AttributeNames=["All"],
            MessageAttributeNames=["All"],
        )

        messages = response.get("Messages", [])
        moved = 0

        for message in messages:
            receipt_handle = message["ReceiptHandle"]
            body = message.get("Body", "")
            attributes = message.get("MessageAttributes", {})

            try:
                self.process_message(body, attributes)
                self.sqs.delete_message(
                    QueueUrl=self.source_queue_url,
                    ReceiptHandle=receipt_handle,
                )
            except Exception as exc:
                self.send_to_dead_letter(message_body=body, original_message=message, error=exc)
                self.sqs.delete_message(
                    QueueUrl=self.source_queue_url,
                    ReceiptHandle=receipt_handle,
                )
                moved += 1

        return moved

    def process_message(self, body: str, message_attributes: dict) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError("Override process_message with your business logic")

    def send_to_dead_letter(self, message_body: str, original_message: dict, error: Exception) -> None:
        attrs = dict(original_message.get("MessageAttributes", {}))
        attrs["deadLetterReason"] = {
            "DataType": "String",
            "StringValue": type(error).__name__,
        }
        attrs["deadLetterError"] = {
            "DataType": "String",
            "StringValue": str(error)[:256],
        }

        self.sqs.send_message(
            QueueUrl=self.dead_letter_queue_url,
            MessageBody=message_body,
            MessageAttributes=attrs,
        )


def main() -> None:
    source_queue_url = os.environ["SQS_SOURCE_QUEUE_URL"]
    dead_letter_queue_url = os.environ["SQS_DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE_URL"]
    region_name = os.getenv("AWS_REGION") or os.getenv("AWS_DEFAULT_REGION")

    messenger = DeadLetterMessenger(
        source_queue_url=source_queue_url,
        dead_letter_queue_url=dead_letter_queue_url,
        region_name=region_name,
    )

    try:
        messenger.receive_and_process(max_messages=int(os.getenv("MAX_MESSAGES", "10")))
    except (BotoCoreError, ClientError) as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"Failed to interact with Amazon SQS: {exc}") from exc


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
